title: Advisory Locks: Application-Level Distributed Locking in Postgres
realWorldScenario: Your microservices backend must execute a monthly interest accrual batch job. Three container instances run concurrently. If two containers run the job simultaneously for the same loan portfolio, interest is doubled.
questionStatement: Compare PostgreSQL Advisory Locks with row-level locks (`SELECT FOR UPDATE`). Explain the differences between session-level and transaction-level advisory locks (`pg_advisory_lock` vs `pg_advisory_xact_lock`), and between blocking and non-blocking variants (`pg_try_advisory_lock`).
expectedConcepts: In-memory lock table without table/row dependency
pg_try_advisory_xact_lock non-blocking semantics for idempotent jobs
PgBouncer transaction-mode danger with session-level advisory locks
hints: What happens if a session-level lock is used with PgBouncer transaction pooling?
Which function returns a boolean immediately instead of blocking?
